history.period: Ancient; discovered around 1251-1252 AD per local tradition
history.summary: An ancient hill temple of Goddess Manudevi, the kuldevi of about 70% of the people of Jalgaon district, set in the scenic Satpura range near Adgaon village in Yawal taluka. The temple is ringed by hills on three sides, with a waterfall and an artificial lake/mini lake in front, and stands at about 500 m altitude, reached by a ~1500 m gravel road plus a ~1500 m trek through forest. Local tradition says the temple was discovered in 1251-1252 AD by Shri K. Pandu Jeevan of the Ingle family; the tired Goddess is believed to have rested at this spot after her battle with Mahishasur, and Lord Parshurama is believed to manifest in the huge trees at the entrance, welcoming pilgrims. A Hanuman shrine stands beside the lake. NOTE (verify): the waterfall's height is reported as 40 ft (apnisanskriti) vs 400 ft (tourmet), and the discovery year as 1251/1252/1259 AD across sources.

name: Satpuda Manudevi Temple
town_description: Yawal is a town in Jalgaon district, about 40-45 km from Jalgaon city, on the edge of the Satpura range; the Manudevi temple lies near Adgaon village in Yawal taluka, off the Yaval-Chopda state highway. The Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary is also nearby. CSV town corrected: 'Jalgaon' is the district; the temple is in Yawal taluka near Adgaon village.

travel.airport: Jalgaon Airport (~40-50 km; no scheduled services as of sources); nearest operating airport Aurangabad (~160 km)
travel.road: Off the Yaval-Chopda state highway, ~9 km from Adgaon-Kasarkheda; ~1-2 hr by taxi or bus from Jalgaon; daily buses and mini-buses run from Jalgaon bus stand; recent development allows vehicles closer to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: June to February (monsoon for the waterfall at its best; winter for the trek)
